questions.q: How is the autoscaling floor actually fixed?
options: Running kubectl edit directly on the live cluster
Changing the Terraform module's profile_name argument from "peak-season" to "standard", through a pull request and terraform plan/apply
Deleting the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler entirely
Manually scaling the deployment down once with no config change
questions.explain: The fix goes through source control and Terraform, the same way the original infrastructure was provisioned, so it doesn't just drift out of sync again.

questions.q: What two pieces of evidence confirm the autoscaling fix actually worked?
options: Only a visual check of the Terraform code
kubectl get hpa showing the corrected replica count AND Azure Cost Analysis showing the forecast settle back toward the original $1,750/month projection
Only a customer confirming the app feels faster
Only the pull request being approved
questions.explain: Both the cluster-level evidence and the cost-level evidence matter; either one alone would be incomplete validation.

questions.q: What replaces the wildcard Principal in the corrected bucket policy?
options: A second wildcard scoped to Driftwood's account only
The specific ARN of the driftwood-backup-writer IAM role
No Principal field at all
Priya Suresh's personal AWS user
questions.explain: The policy is scoped to the one role that actually needs access, replacing "*" with a specific role ARN.

questions.q: What AWS CLI call confirms the bucket is no longer publicly accessible?
options: aws s3 ls
aws s3api get-bucket-policy-status, checking for "IsPublic": false
aws ec2 describe-instances
aws iam list-roles
questions.explain: get-bucket-policy-status reports AWS's own determination of whether the bucket's effective policy is public.

questions.q: Why does Theo also re-check that the Lesson 7 replication job still works after tightening the policy?
options: It's not necessary once the policy JSON looks correct
To confirm the tightened policy didn't accidentally lock out the one principal that's supposed to have access, since a fix that breaks the job it's protecting isn't a real fix
Because the replication job is unrelated and doesn't need checking
To test a completely different feature
questions.explain: A security fix that silently breaks the legitimate backup job isn't actually validated — both the security outcome and the operational outcome need confirming.
